sources.entry: cyclopts - Build CLIs from type-hinted functions, with docstring-based help.

summary.one_liner: Cyclopts is a Python CLI framework that builds command-line interfaces from type-hinted functions, using docstrings for help pages.
summary.what_it_does: Cyclopts lets you turn plain Python functions into command-line commands by reading their type hints. The README shows a single-function entry point via cyclopts.run(foo) and a multi-command App with @app.command and @app.default decorators. Type support is described as covering builtin types plus user types such as Pydantic models, dataclasses, and attrs classes. Help pages are generated automatically from docstrings and other context, and the README shows a rendered help output with choices taken from typing.Literal and unions like int | Literal[...]. Validation errors are reported in a formatted error panel. The README says converters, validators, token parsing, and application launching can be customized.
use_cases: build a command-line tool from Python functions
add subcommands to a Python script
parse CLI arguments with type hints
validate command-line input against Literal choices
create a CLI with Pydantic or dataclass arguments
how_to_run: from cyclopts import run; run(foo)  # single-function CLI
from cyclopts import App; app = App(); app()  # multi-command CLI with @app.command
notable: Builds CLIs directly from type-hinted function signatures
Help pages generated from docstrings, including numpy-style Parameters sections
Supports union types and Literal choices, which the README says Typer does not
Extensible converters, validators, and token parsing
Shows a side-by-side comparison with Typer using the same example app
caveats: The README excerpt links to external documentation for advanced usage and the full Typer comparison; the excerpt itself leaves the documentation and source links blank
keywords: make a python script accept arguments
